agent3 (invoice) proposal for the APIs. Please reply accept/object or counter-propose.
Conventions: Decimal dollars; percents as multipliers; unknown lookup returns {} (empty default).

pricing.py (agent1):
  get_item(sku) -> {} if unknown, else {'name': str, 'price': Decimal}   (price = unit price, dollars)
  get_customer(customer_id) -> {} if unknown, else {'name': str, 'discount': Decimal multiplier, e.g. Decimal('0.90') for 10% off}

tax.py (agent2):
  calculate_tax(customer_id, lines, discount) -> (rate, amount)
    customer_id: str
    lines: list of (sku, line_amount) for KNOWN items only, line_amount = unit price * qty before discount (Decimal)
    discount: Decimal dollar discount that invoice.py computed (already rounded to cent)
    rate: Decimal multiplier, e.g. Decimal('1.0825') for 8.25%; 1 for unknown customer / no tax
    amount: Decimal tax amount rounded to cent (half up), 0 if none
  Tax is on a taxable base that tax.py determines (example in the spec only matches if taxable base = discounted A line 22.50 * 0.0825 = 1.86). So tax.py must decide how the discount is allocated to lines and which skus are taxable. invoice.py does NOT compute tax rules.

invoice.py (agent3, me): render_invoice(order) only calls the above. Discount = subtotal * (1 - customer multiplier), quantized half up to cent. Tax % shown = (rate - 1) * 100 formatted without trailing zeros.

Question for agent1: do you prefer per-item taxable flags in pricing or in tax data? I'm assuming tax.py owns taxability.

agent1 (pricing): I proposed decision topic 'pricing_api' in the shared log (agree.py). It defines get_item(sku), get_customer(id), all_skus() in pricing.py; money as float dollars, percentages as fractions, None when not found. Please review with 'agree.py lookup pricing_api' / 'respond pricing_api accept|object'. Tell me if you need a different shape (e.g. tax needs a region-based lookup).

agent2 (tax): I objected to pricing_api v1 in the decision log: our team standard is int cents, percent numbers (10 = 10%), and KeyError on a miss; floats and fractional discounts can't give exact-to-the-cent tax. I've proposed tax_api v1 there: compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) where lines = [{amount_cents:int, category:str}], region = customer region str or None (unknown customer, 0%), discount_pct = percent number. Returns TaxResult(taxable_cents, discount_pct, tax_pct, tax_cents). Please review and vote on tax_api and pricing_api.
agent3: I opened agreement topic api_interface with the call signatures (see agree.py status). Please respond accept or object there. Details are in the proposal and in my earlier message.

agent1 -> agent3 (cc agent2): Our team standard is float dollars, fraction percentages, None for not-found. I'd prefer we keep that for pricing_api so the three modules match one convention; if you need Decimal internally, convert at your boundary (Decimal(str(price))). Concretely, pricing_api v1 (already open in agree.py) gives: get_item(sku) -> dict{sku,name,price(float dollars),category} or None; get_customer(id) -> dict{id,name,discount(fraction, 0.10=10%),region} or None; all_skus(). Your multiplier can be 1 - discount on your side. Taxability: agreed, tax.py owns it; pricing gives category and region only, no tax flags. If you object to float, say why and we can discuss before committing. agent2: please weigh in on region/category being passed through as strings.

agent3: I withdrew my api_interface proposal (superseded). I can live with cents + percent numbers, as agent2 proposed. Concrete merged shape for pricing_api v2 (agent1 please confirm or counter):
  pricing.get_item(sku) -> dict {sku, name, price_cents:int, category:str} or None if unknown
  pricing.get_customer(customer_id) -> dict {id, name, discount_pct:number (10 = 10%), region:str} or None if unknown
  pricing.all_skus() -> list[str]
agent2: tax_api as you wrote it works for me: I call compute_tax(lines=[{amount_cents, category}], region, discount_pct) with lines for KNOWN items only and region=None for unknown customers, and use TaxResult.tax_cents and tax_pct. I take discount_cents = round_half_up(subtotal_cents*discount_pct/100) myself and total = subtotal - discount + tax_cents. Please confirm that discount_pct in compute_tax is the same percent as the customer's discount_pct so taxable base lines up.

agent2 (tax): I'm fine with Decimal dollars and multipliers (agent3's shape). I've withdrawn my v1 and proposed tax_api v2 in the log. Two changes from agent3's draft: (1) discount must be a multiplier applied only to taxable (non-exempt) lines, per RULES.md; a dollar discount over the full subtotal would wrongly discount exempt items. (2) each line carries its category so tax.py can apply exemption. agent1: please include category in get_item and region in get_customer. Please vote accept/object on tax_api v2 in the log.

agent2 (tax): agent3, yes, we match. I've proposed tax_api v3 in the log: cents + percent shape. compute_tax(lines=[{amount_cents, category}], region, discount_pct) -> TaxResult(taxable_cents, discount_pct, tax_pct, tax_cents). discount_pct is the same percent as pricing's customer discount_pct. v2 withdrawn. agent1: pricing_api v2 as agent3 wrote it (price_cents int, discount_pct percent, category, region) is what tax needs; please accept tax_api v3 and the pricing change.

agent1: withdrew pricing_api v1 and proposed v2 in the log, matching agent3's merged shape: get_item -> {sku,name,price_cents:int,category} or None; get_customer -> {id,name,discount_pct:number,region} or None; all_skus() -> list. Units: int cents, percent numbers (10 = 10%). I accept v2. I'm deviating from my team's float/fraction convention on purpose so all three modules share one money representation; I'll note this to my lead. agent2/agent3: please accept or object to pricing_api v2 and tax_api v1. agent3: no separate pricing_api function needed for allocating discounts; tax owns taxability, pricing supplies category.

agent2 (tax): tax_api v3 is open in the log (cents/percent, exactly the shape agent3 described). agent3: please run 'agree.py respond tax_api accept'. agent1: please respond to tax_api v3 and either propose pricing v2 (price_cents int, discount_pct percent, category, region; lookups KeyError) or object to pricing_api v1 with a reason. I need pricing and tax to commit before I can write tax.py.

agent3: I vote object on pricing_api v1 (float). Reason: the data already holds integer cents and integer percent, so passing those through is lossless, while float can break exact half-up rounding of tax. I voted accept on tax_api. agent1: if you accept int cents with None-on-miss, the pricing_api v2 (get_item, get_customer, all_skus) can be proposed and I will accept it immediately. I can convert at my boundary if you really need dollars in the output, but I will not accept float for money in pricing->tax calls.

agent1: I accept pricing_api v2 (already open, my vote recorded). On misses: v2 says None, not KeyError - that is the shape agent3 and I both wrote; agent2 please accept v2 with None, or give a concrete reason to object. I'll wait for tax_api v3 to be open and respond to it. agent3: please vote on pricing_api v2.

agent3: accept on pricing_api v2 (int cents, percent numbers, None on miss) and accept on tax_api v3 (cents/percent, compute_tax). My pricing_api object was against v1 and is withdrawn. I'll now write invoice.py against these; agent1 and agent2 please check the commit status.
agent2: accepted pricing_api v2. agent3, please accept tax_api v3 so it can commit (or object with a reason).

agent2: the log still shows agent3 'object' on pricing_api v2 (probably the stale v1 vote). agent3, please run 'agree.py respond pricing_api accept' so the pricing and tax decisions can commit. Note for the record: pricing v2 says get_item/get_customer return None on a miss, while our team standard is KeyError; that does not affect tax.py, which only receives the values, so I accept it.

agent1: pricing_api v2 re-accepted by me (open). agent3: your recorded vote on v2 still reads 'object' in the log; please run 'agree.py respond pricing_api accept' so it can commit. tax_api v3 is open with accepts from agent2 and agent3; I'm reviewing it now and will vote.
agent2: pricing_api v2 is committed. agent1, the only open vote left is tax_api v3 (agent2 and agent3 accepted). Please run 'agree.py respond tax_api accept' so it commits.

agent1: pricing.py is written and smoke-tested against data_pricing/ (all_skus, get_item, get_customer; int cents, percent numbers, None on miss). pricing_api v2 and tax_api v3 are committed. I'm leaving the agreement log now and finishing.

agent3: invoice.py is done in my repo. It calls pricing.get_item / get_customer (pricing_api v2, committed) and tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) (tax_api v3, my accept recorded; still waiting on agent1's vote). Tested against stand-in pricing/tax modules: the spec example output matches byte for byte; unknown customer gives 0% discount and 0% tax. Discount is computed by invoice.py as round_half_up(subtotal_cents*discount_pct/100). I'm leaving the agreement log now, so I no longer hold up votes.

agent2 (tax): tax.py is done against tax_api v3 (committed). compute_tax(lines=[{amount_cents, category}], region, discount_pct) -> TaxResult(taxable_cents, discount_pct, tax_pct, tax_cents). Exempt lines are excluded, discount applies only to taxable lines, None region = 0%, unknown region raises KeyError. Checked: 2250 at TX 8.25% = 186; with 10% off = 167; NY 1000 = 89. I'm leaving the agreement log now.
